doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

title: New album, Timber Ridge and hurricane damage to family
summary: Pete discusses the new album, a land investment, and his parents riding out the hurricane in Biloxi, causing a cancelled concert and lawsuit.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was wondering if I understood right if Pete was making it, recording a new record album, and I wondered when it would be out and if he had a name for it.
Well, the new one's out now. It's called Boatsides now.
I've got it for Christmas. I thought you said you were making it.
Yeah. The new one should be out, I'd say, in about three weeks. I just got a call yesterday about it.
And we recorded in Las Vegas with my group I have here in New Orleans.
And also, I wondered about Timber Ridge. If you still had it or if it was?

Yeah, well, so far, we've just gone through a little legal thing with them now, but we're still involved in it. It's not all mine. It's just when you put your name to something, we checked it over, and it's wonderful land over there, and it was high. It didn't get too much damage during the storm.
I was wondering about your folks, how they came out.
They came out fine. My dad's a lot better. He was a nervous wreck for a while, but he's... He was quite a bloat. Yeah, he was, you know, but he's real fine, thank you.
No, thank you, ma'am. All right, thank you.
Thank you. Well, what happened to your folks?

Well, they were in the storm. They rode out the storm in Biloxi. Oh. So they were over there in their summer home, and the water was over the roof. But they went to one of my cousins' house, and we went to pick them up. And we stayed and we went to pick them up, and everything, you know, it's just so funny how people up in the country are... We were supposed to do a concert in Madison, Wisconsin. And they couldn't believe that we had a storm. And I had to cancel out. One of the first ones I've canceled out in all the years, I've only canceled one because we couldn't get through with snow on the bus, and this one here. And they sued me for $30,000. Oh. And they can't, you know, so we have to go through the laws, and the film of the coast, and I might have to fly up there with, you know... They didn't hear about it. I don't think they did. I was just wondering.
